title: Near-infrared magnetic linear and non-reciprocal directional dichroism in the chiral antiferromagnet SmFe3(BO3)4
authors: B. Beke, B. Szász, I. A. Gudim, D. Szaller, S. Bordács
abstract: We investigated the influence of antiferromagnetic (AFM) order on the near-infrared optical re- sponse of SmFe3(BO3)4 by polarization-resolved, magneto-optical spectroscopy. Below the Néel temperature, we observed pronounced magnetic linear dichroism at the 4f -4f transitions of Sm3+. By rotating the order parameter of the easy-plane AFM ground state using magnetic fields, we demonstrated the magnetic field control of linear dichroism, and deduced polarization selection rules. In addition, we detected non-reciprocal directional dichroism for several 4f -4f transitions. The non-reciprocal absorption appears in the symmetry-allowed toroidal geometry when the in- plane magnetic field is normal to one of the two-fold rotation axes. These results indicate a strong interference between electric- and magnetic-dipole excitations for transitions showing non-reciprocal absorption. The observed optical anisotropies provide a promising path to detect the in-plane orien- tation of the AFM order, enabling imaging and time-resolved studies of the AFM order parameter in rare-earth ferroborates.
summary: This experimental study uses polarization-resolved infrared spectroscopy to probe the optical response of the antiferromagnet SmFe3(BO3)4. The researchers successfully measured magnetic linear and non-reciprocal directional dichroism, demonstrating that these optical anisotropies are highly sensitive to the orientation of the AFM order parameter. This work opens a pathway for optically imaging and studying the magnetic ordering in rare-earth borates.
main_problem: The study investigates how antiferromagnetic (AFM) order influences the near-infrared optical response of the chiral antiferromagnet SmFe3(BO3)4.
main_result: The researchers observed magnetic linear and non-reciprocal directional dichroism (NDD) in the 4f-4f transitions, confirming strong interference between electric- and magnetic-dipole excitations.
method: Polarization-resolved, magneto-optical spectroscopy using infrared transmission measurements on single crystals.
model_or_system: The physical system is the chiral antiferromagnet SmFe3(BO3)4, where the AFM order parameter is constrained to the easy-plane. The analysis relies on symmetry considerations linking the AFM order to optical responses.
key_observables: Magnetic linear dichroism, non-reciprocal directional dichroism (NDD), and the magnetoelectric tensor components.
important_parameters: Temperature relative to the Néel temperature ($T_N$), applied magnetic field strength and orientation ($\mathbf{B}$), and light polarization ($\mathbf{E}_\omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the AFM order parameter dictates the optical anisotropy and that the observed NDD is linked to the presence of a toroidal moment.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure and the magnetic field dependence of the absorption spectra, showing polarization-resolved measurements and difference spectra ($\alpha(+B) - \alpha(-B)$) that confirm NDD.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework linking AFM order to optical responses, then presenting measurements of linear dichroism, and finally focusing on the detection and interpretation of non-reciprocal directional dichroism as a probe for the toroidal moment.
why_interesting: The detection of NDD in the infrared range provides a novel, optically accessible method to probe the orientation and dynamics of the AFM order parameter in rare-earth materials, linking magnetic structure to electronic excitations.
